plan.angle: The top 10 are tool listicles and general guides that name categories of work without showing one running. This page shows four small businesses with one workflow each, written down to the trigger, the rule, the number and the person who handles the exception: a furnace request that waits too long, an invoice past due, a signed proposal, and coffee stock below its reorder point. Each is built as one app with its own database, and the how-to tells an owner which workflow to build first.
tab_stories: Drumhallow Heating and Air gets a web request for a furnace repair from zip code 30318 at 9:40 a.m.; the app gives it to Hollis Harbottle, the tech who covers that zip, and when nobody has marked it contacted by 11:40 a.m., the owner, Gideon Tregarthen, gets a Slack alert.

Thimbleby Lawn and Garden's app reads open invoices from QuickBooks every morning; invoice #2216 to Pettifer Court HOA for $1,480 is 14 days past due and gets its second reminder email, and at 21 days past due it becomes a call task for the owner, Wilhelmina Chaudry.

Caddick Design Studio's client Ridley Park Orthodontics accepts a $9,600 proposal; the app emails the client an intake questionnaire and gives the project lead, Corisande Velling, a kickoff task, and if the questionnaire is still blank after 3 days, the client gets a reminder.

Kestlemoor Coffee Roasters logs each roast, and when Colombian green coffee drops to 48 kg against a 60 kg reorder point, the app drafts a 120 kg reorder and sends it to the owner, Bram Okonjo-Wilde, to approve in the app.
